title: AP Precalculus — Logarithms Practice
question: 12 logarithm questions in three groups: Easy (evaluate, base 10, log of 1, change the form), Medium (fraction exponent, input below 1, estimate, solve), Hard (product, power and quotient rules, change of base, decibels).
intro:
**12 questions: 4 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.** Rules to keep in mind:

- \(\log_b c = a \iff b^{a} = c\); no base written means base \(10\).
- \(\log_b 1 = 0\), \(\log_b b = 1\); an input between \(0\) and \(1\) gives a negative log.
- \(\log_b (mn) = \log_b m + \log_b n\), \(\log_b \frac{m}{n} = \log_b m - \log_b n\), \(\log_b m^{k} = k\log_b m\).
- Change of base: \(\log_b c = \dfrac{\log c}{\log b}\).

**A calculator is allowed. Show your calculation before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: Evaluate a power of 2
Base 10
questions.prompt:
No base written means base \(10\). Find

\[
\log 1000
\]

questions.title: Log of 1
questions.solution_title: Any base to the power 0 is 1

questions.title: Exponential form to log form
questions.prompt:
Which equation means the same as

\[
3^4 = 81
\]
questions.solution_title: Base stays the base, the exponent is the answer
questions.solution:
\[
b^{a} = c \iff \log_b c = a
\]

- Base \(b = 3\)
- Exponent \(a = 4\) is the value of the log
- Result \(c = 81\) is the input

\[
\boxed{\log_3 81 = 4}
\]

- Not \(\log_4 81 = 3\): \(4\) is the exponent, it cannot be the base.
- Not \(\log_3 4 = 81\): the input of the log is the result \(81\), not the exponent.

questions.title: A fraction exponent
Input below 1
questions.solution_title: A fraction needs a negative exponent

questions.title: Estimate between two integers
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
3^3 &= 27 \\
3^4 &= 81
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
27 < 50 < 81
\]

So the exponent sits between \(3\) and \(4\):

\[
\boxed{3 < \log_3 50 < 4}
\]

- A calculator gives \(\log_3 50 \approx 3.56\).
- Not \(\tfrac{50}{3}\): a log is an exponent, not a division.

questions.title: Solve an exponential equation
questions.solution_title: Rewrite as a log, or match powers of 5

questions.title: Product rule
questions.solution:
\[
\log_b m + \log_b n = \log_b (mn)
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
\log_6 9 + \log_6 4 &= \log_6 (9\cdot4) \\
&= \log_6 36 \\
&= \boxed{2}
\end{aligned}
\]

- \(6^2 = 36\), so the log is \(2\).
- Not \(\log_6 13\): the product rule multiplies the inputs; it never adds them.
- Not \(36\): that is the input of the final log, not its value.

questions.title: Power rule and quotient rule
questions.solution_title: Evaluate each log, or use the rules

questions.title: Change of base
questions.prompt:
Use a calculator. To 2 decimal places,

\[
\log_5 40 \approx\ ?
\]
questions.solution_title: Divide two logs of the same kind
questions.solution:
\[
\log_b c = \frac{\log c}{\log b} = \frac{\ln c}{\ln b}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
\log_5 40 &= \frac{\log 40}{\log 5} \\
&\approx \frac{1.602}{0.699} \\
&\approx \boxed{2.29}
\end{aligned}
\]

Sense check: \(5^2 = 25 < 40 < 125 = 5^3\), so the answer is between \(2\) and \(3\).

- Not \(8\): that is \(40\div5\).
- Not \(1.60\): that is \(\log 40\) alone (base 10). Divide by \(\log 5\).
- Not \(0.44\): the fraction is upside down, \(\frac{\log 5}{\log 40}\).

questions.title: Decibels: a log scale
questions.prompt:
Loudness in decibels is

\[
L = 10\log\!\left(\frac{P}{P_0}\right)
\]

where \(P\) is the sound power.

- A drill measures \(100\) dB.
- A conversation measures \(70\) dB.

How many times more power does the drill have?
questions.solution_title: Every 10 dB is a factor of 10

takeaway: A logarithm is an exponent. Every rule on this page is a rule about exponents written backwards.
